title: Helicone returns SSE for a tool-enabled chat completion
user_action: A first-class agent sends a tool-enabled chat-completions request through Calciforge with stream=true.
promise: A valid upstream streaming response must not become an agent timeout or model-unavailable error.
aggression_vectors: split content across several SSE frames
split tool-call arguments across several SSE frames
preserve stream=true on the outbound request
return an SSE content type with parameters

title: First-class agent model traffic stays on the Calciforge gateway path
user_action: A managed OpenClaw, Hermes, or other first-class agent handles a normal chat message.
promise: For first-class adapters, provider/model traffic should go through Calciforge unless the operator explicitly opts out.
aggression_vectors: agent service has stale proxy environment
agent config points directly at a provider
agent sends server-side web-search tool traffic
doctor is run against a different config path than the service

title: Hostile fetched content is blocked on the response path
user_action: An agent fetches or summarizes a page containing prompt-injection canary text.
promise: The model should not receive forbidden fetched content merely because the URL was allowed to load.
aggression_vectors: forbidden text appears only in the HTTP response body
forbidden text appears in JSON returned by a provider-side web tool
the request itself is harmless but the returned content is not
the body is compressed or has a misleading content type

title: Packaged services use the same config paths that doctor validates
user_action: An operator installs or updates Calciforge via Homebrew or Docker Compose, then sends a real channel message.
promise: An install that passes doctor should not run a different binary, config file, vault path, or helper script at runtime.
aggression_vectors: legacy ~/.calciforge path remains present
launchd has an older binary path
Docker volume lacks a helper script
rsync or runtime binary is missing during update

title: Local model routes stay inside a usable latency envelope
user_action: A user sends a short prompt to a first-class agent backed by a local Ollama model.
promise: A local default should feel responsive, and slow paths should be measured and visible instead of looking dead.
aggression_vectors: model is cold
model is loaded with a very large context window
agent includes a large session preamble
the route makes multiple model calls before replying
